notes: RUN RECORDS ARE NEVER OVERWRITTEN — attempt-suffixed archives, bare file = latest. THE DEFECT (observed 2026-08-22): tools/runner wrote untracked/runs/<task>.json at launch and REWROTE the same path at exit; a re-dispatch of the same task REWROTE the path AGAIN, destroying the previous attempt's telemetry (wall, exit, kill reason, tokens, session). When the operator asked to confirm the 12:47Z Claude session-limit outage, the run records for T615/T621/T622 no longer described the kills — the re-runs had replaced them; the kills survived only in docs/infra/dispatch-heals.jsonl (append-only) and the .log files. Ruling 32 (2026-08-22) requires guard-killed rows PRESENT and labeled censored; an overwritten killed attempt is a dropped one, silently, by the mechanism that should preserve it. THE FIX (chosen: attempt-suffixed files, the bundle's Option A variant): the bare untracked/runs/<task>.json ALWAYS holds the LATEST attempt; when a new attempt starts, the previous bare record is renamed (atomic os.replace — NOT a copy or symlink, which would double-count in the AC7 census that iterates every file) to untracked/runs/<task>.<N>.json where N is the attempt number it carried. Attempt numbering is 'from the existing count': first dispatch of a task = attempt 1 (bare only — single-attempt rows are byte-identical to pre-T650), Nth dispatch = attempt N. Every record carries an explicit 'attempt' field and a 'model' field parsed from the dispatch command's --model flag, so attempts are distinguishable at a glance (the full dispatch remains in 'command'). WHY NOT JSONL: every existing reader opens untracked/runs/<task>.json as a single JSON object — dispatch_verify.read_run_record, attribution-backfill.parse_run_model, the brief-telemetry/taskid/claude-liveness/agent-progress/orphan-reaper regressions; the Zig reader (managent readRunRecords + latestRunRecordFor) already iterates ALL *.json files and picks the latest by 'start', so multiple files per task need no Zig change. READERS ON THE NEW LAYOUT: dispatch_verify.read_run_record reads the bare = LATEST attempt (the run it is verifying — correct); attribution-backfill reads the bare = latest dispatch's command (correct); managent reap/resume use latestRunRecordFor = latest by start = the bare (correct — reap confirmed against a scratch store, evidence names the latest attempt's exit/signal); the AC7 wall-kill census (orcha-acceptance.sh) iterates every file and now sees each killed attempt EXACTLY ONCE (before T650 the re-dispatch erased it; a copy/symlink of the latest would double-count — the rename scheme avoids both). p95 COMPUTATION (T634/T643 dependency) — decision: count COMPLETED attempts ONLY; a killed attempt's wall is censored (Ruling 32), not a sample of how long the work takes. The filter is explicit in the regression (records with a wall and no killed/killed_by/signal), not emergent. RED QUOTE (pre-fix, HEAD tools/runner, regression arm A): after wall-kill + re-dispatch, 'FAIL: no archived untracked/runs/T6501.1.json (the killed attempt is GONE — the pre-T650 defect)' — the first attempt's record did not survive. GREEN (fixed runner): bare = attempt 2 exit=0, archived .1.json = attempt 1 signal=9 killed_by=wall with the full kill reason — both records readable. Three attempts -> T6502.1/T6502.2/T6502.json with attempt numbers 1,2,3 correctly ordered. Null control: single dispatch leaves exactly one record, dispatch_verify.read_run_record returns the same shape as pre-T650. KNOWN GAP (recorded per the brief): the seat re-dispatched T635 — a watchdog-killed row — BEFORE this row existed, overwriting the killed attempt's run record. That loss is real and NOT recoverable; T526's record was likewise overwritten by a later re-dispatch (the kill is proven only by untracked/log/t526.log '[runner] KILL: progress timeout 600s' at wall 1129.6 s, and T635's by untracked/log/t635.log + exit 124 in 1732.6 s). Do not let a future reader assume those files were always this way. Also left as-is per 'do not migrate or rewrite historical records': untracked/runs/T555.json is malformed (two JSON docs concatenated, 5111 bytes — a pre-atomic-writer torn write), reported by managent as '1 unparseable or malformed run record(s)'; it predates this change and is not migrated. COLLISION RESOLUTION: T643 (progress-watchdog, deepseek-v4-pro) held tools/runner; its runner was killed by the very 600s watchdog it was fixing (untracked/runs/T643.json: killed='progress timeout 600s', signal 9, killed_by=watchdog, wall 1706.8 s, end 2026-08-22T17:08:53Z; runner pid 2508 dead) and its row was never closed. managent reap classified it [ORPHAN]; T650 reaped it (verdict abandoned, evidence in the note) and PRESERVED its complete-but-uncommitted work to untracked/T643-inflight/ (runner diff + build.zig diff + full file copies + README; its findings/T643-*.json and tools/regression-runner-agent-progress.sh remain on disk) so a successor can land it. T650's tools/runner commit therefore contains ONLY T650's changes (T643's watchdog work was reverted from the tree after preservation to avoid misattribution). Landmark: advances L1 (measurement integrity) — the run-record census no longer loses a guard-killed attempt to its own retry; gates re-dispatch of killed rows.
